newsitem.title: ITALY: Lira rejoins ERM but no guarantee on EMU.
newsitem.headline: Lira rejoins ERM but no guarantee on EMU.

text.p: Italy returned to Europe's Exchange Rate Mechanism on Monday, four years after crashing out of the currency grid, but it still faces an uphill battle to join the first wave of nations in a single European currency.
Two days of tough bargaining in Brussels ended on Sunday night with EU finance ministers and central bank governors agreeing to let the lira back into the exchange mechanism (ERM).

Italian financial markets reacted to the news by marking stocks and bond futures higher in early trade, but the buoyant reaction was already waning when reports of judicial problems for Prime Minister Romano Prodi jolted investors.
Some of Italy's 14 partners in the European Union (EU) were making clear, too, that rejoining the ERM was no guarantee Italy would make the economic grade for a single European currency.
Despite that, Prodi hailed the move as a "fundamental step" towards Italy becoming a founder member of the EU's economic and monetary union when it is launched in 1999.
"To have brought the lira into Europe is the consequence of the seriousness of our economic policy and the stability we have given the country," Italy's ANSA news agency quoted him as saying.
The lira spent most of the day trading around its new central parity rate in the ERM of 990 lire to the mark. That compares with 999.15 in late European trading on Friday.

But share traders in Milan said stocks began to slide as the stock market digested the likely impact of the 990 lire rate -- tougher for Italian exporters than the 1,000 lire plus rate that Italian officials fought for in Brussels.
"We are worried by the 990 lire parity level, we will have to measure up to this new exchange rate" said Giorgio Fossa, president of the Italian employers association, Confindustria.

Milan's all-share Mibtel index put on 0.7 percent in early trade but reversed gear and closed 0.48 percent down at 10,492 points on reports that a Rome magistrate had asked for Prodi to be charged with abuse of office when he headed state industrial holding company IRI in 1993.
Italian Btp bond futures, which hit new historic highs in morning trade, also retreated on the report.

"There's no euphoria with people saying the future's rosy now we're back in. The market looks slightly overbought technically and some consolidation is expected," said Oriano Moro, a trader at Gestnord brokers in Milan.
Joining the ERM, although an important milestone along the road to a single currency, leaves Italy with a big job to meet the economc criteria for EMU.

Its hardest task will be to get the public sector deficit down to three percent of gross domestic product (GDP) by the end of 1997 -- one of the key Maastricht Treaty conditions for joining the single currency project.
The European Union will decide in early 1998 which of the bloc's 15 members will be allowed into the magic circle of countries forming a single currency the following year.

Italy is set to overshoot its deficit target this year by a wide margin, but is pinning its hopes of narrowing the gap on a very tough 1997 budget and rapid fall in interest rates. Lower rates would cut the cost of servicing the country's debt mountain -- the largest component of the deficit.
Analysts said it remained unclear whether the negotiations over the lira offered any clue over how the EU would look upon an EMU area that includes a large number of members.

German central bank president Hans Tietmeyer and his Duitch counterpart Wim Duisenberg stressed after Sunday's meeting that membership of the ERM would not prejudge the decision in early 1998 on which countries participated in the single currency.
Germany, which has fought for months to ensure there is no softening in the Maastricht criteria to allow in countries like Spain and Italy, got some support from Austria.

"It is not serious if Italy joins one or two years later," Finance Minister Viktor Klima told Austrian state radio. "But of course it is the goal of the Italian government as well as the European Union and Austria that Italy joins the euro-zone as soon as possible."
